9	/-!
10	# Mayer-Vietoris LES core for `ModuleCat k`-valued sheaf cohomology
11	
12	This file (iter-063 split, cohort 1) contains the MV LES core for
13	`Sheaf J (ModuleCat k)`-valued cohomology: the Mathlib gap-fill
14	`Abelian.Ext.chgUnivLinearEquiv` plus the iter-016 → iter-026 abstract
15	Mayer-Vietoris infrastructure (`HModule'_cohomologyPresheafFunctor`,
16	`HModule'_toBiprod`, `HModule'_fromBiprod`, `HModule'_δ`, `HModule'_sequence`,
17	`HModule'_sequence_exact`, and the `δ`-zero simp companions).
18	
19	This is cohort 1 of the original `MayerVietoris.lean` split:
20	* `MayerVietorisCore.lean` (this file): MV LES core + Mathlib gap-fill.
21	* `MayerVietorisCover.lean`: 2-affine cover MV + cover-totality bridges +
22	  `IsCechAcyclicCover` consumers + `HasAffineCechAcyclicCover` carrier.
23	
24	See `blueprint/src/chapters/Cohomology_MayerVietoris.tex`.
25	-/
26	
27	set_option autoImplicit false
28	
29	universe u v w w'
30	
31	open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace AlgebraicGeometry
32	
33	/-! ## Iter-034 Mathlib gap-fill: `Abelian.Ext.chgUniv` as a `LinearEquiv`
34	
35	Mathlib's `Abelian.Ext.chgUniv : Ext.{w} X Y n ≃ Ext.{w'} X Y n`
36	(`Mathlib/Algebra/Homology/DerivedCategory/Ext/Basic.lean` L540) is a bare
37	`Equiv` only. The iter-034 universe-bridge `HModule'_eq_HModule_linearEquiv`
38	(below in `section CoverTotality`) requires it as a `LinearEquiv` over the
39	`Linear R C`-enriched abelian category. The upgrade is mechanical: the
40	`AddCommGroup (Ext X Y n)` and `Module R (Ext X Y n)` instances are themselves
41	transferred from the standard derived category through `homEquiv`, and
42	Mathlib's load-bearing intermediate lemma `Ext.homEquiv_chgUniv` (Basic.lean
43	L543–545) shows that `chgUniv` preserves the underlying derived-category
44	morphism. So `chgUniv` automatically commutes with `+` and `•`. Two short
45	helper lemmas (`chgUniv_add` and `chgUniv_smul`) plus a 7-line `LinearEquiv`
46	structure literal give the upgrade.
47	
48	This cohort lives outside `namespace AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme` because the
49	helpers belong to the `CategoryTheory.Abelian.Ext` namespace. We use the
50	qualified-name pattern `Abelian.Ext.foo` rather than wrapping the entire file
51	in a second namespace block. -/
52	
53	/-- Iter-034 Mathlib gap-fill (a): `Abelian.Ext.chgUniv` is additive. The
54	underlying `homEquiv` (`Mathlib/Algebra/Homology/DerivedCategory/Ext/Basic.lean`
55	L162) is preserved by `chgUniv` (Mathlib lemma `Ext.homEquiv_chgUniv`,
56	L543–545), and the `AddCommGroup (Ext X Y n)` instance (L241–243) is defined by
57	transferring the `AddCommGroup` from the standard derived category through
58	`homEquiv`. Combining these via the `Ext.ext` extensionality (L177–179) gives
59	additivity. -/
60	private lemma Abelian.Ext.chgUniv_add
61	    {C : Type*} [Category C] [Abelian C]
62	    [HasExt.{w} C] [HasExt.{w'} C] {X Y : C} {n : ℕ} (a b : Abelian.Ext.{w} X Y n) :
63	    Abelian.Ext.chgUniv.{w'} (a + b) =
64	      Abelian.Ext.chgUniv.{w'} a + Abelian.Ext.chgUniv.{w'} b := by
65	  letI := HasDerivedCategory.standard C
66	  ext
67	  rw [Abelian.Ext.add_hom, ← Abelian.Ext.homAddEquiv_apply,
68	      ← Abelian.Ext.homAddEquiv_apply, ← Abelian.Ext.homAddEquiv_apply]
69	  change Abelian.Ext.homEquiv (Abelian.Ext.chgUniv.{w'} (a + b)) =
70	    Abelian.Ext.homEquiv (Abelian.Ext.chgUniv.{w'} a) +
71	      Abelian.Ext.homEquiv (Abelian.Ext.chgUniv.{w'} b)
72	  rw [Abelian.Ext.homEquiv_chgUniv, Abelian.Ext.homEquiv_chgUniv,
73	      Abelian.Ext.homEquiv_chgUniv, ← Abelian.Ext.add_hom]
74	
75	/-- Iter-034 Mathlib gap-fill (b): `Abelian.Ext.chgUniv` is `R`-linear when `C`
76	is `Linear R`-enriched. Same proof shape as `chgUniv_add`, but using
77	`smul_hom` (`Mathlib/Algebra/Homology/DerivedCategory/Ext/Linear.lean` L52–55)
78	in place of `add_hom`. -/
79	private lemma Abelian.Ext.chgUniv_smul
80	    {R : Type*} [Ring R] {C : Type*} [Category C] [Abelian C] [Linear R C]
81	    [HasExt.{w} C] [HasExt.{w'} C] {X Y : C} {n : ℕ}
82	    (r : R) (a : Abelian.Ext.{w} X Y n) :
83	    Abelian.Ext.chgUniv.{w'} (r • a) = r • Abelian.Ext.chgUniv.{w'} a := by
84	  letI := HasDerivedCategory.standard C
85	  ext
86	  rw [Abelian.Ext.smul_hom, ← Abelian.Ext.homAddEquiv_apply,
87	      ← Abelian.Ext.homAddEquiv_apply]
88	  change Abelian.Ext.homEquiv (Abelian.Ext.chgUniv.{w'} (r • a)) =
89	    r • Abelian.Ext.homEquiv (Abelian.Ext.chgUniv.{w'} a)
90	  rw [Abelian.Ext.homEquiv_chgUniv, Abelian.Ext.homEquiv_chgUniv,
91	      ← Abelian.Ext.smul_hom]
92	
93	/-- Iter-034 Mathlib gap-fill (c): the `R`-linear upgrade of Mathlib's bare-`Equiv`
94	`Abelian.Ext.chgUniv : Ext.{w} X Y n ≃ Ext.{w'} X Y n` to a `LinearEquiv`,
95	when `C` is `Linear R`-enriched abelian. Combines (a) and (b). The
96	`Mathlib/Algebra/Homology/DerivedCategory/Ext/Basic.lean` L540 declaration is
97	universe-polymorphic but only proves the underlying bijection; this wrapper
98	adds the algebraic structure preservation needed for downstream `LinearEquiv`
99	chaining (specifically, the iter-034 universe bridge
100	`HModule'_eq_HModule_linearEquiv` below). -/
101	noncomputable def Abelian.Ext.chgUnivLinearEquiv
102	    {R : Type*} [Ring R] {C : Type*} [Category C] [Abelian C] [Linear R C]
103	    [HasExt.{w} C] [HasExt.{w'} C] {X Y : C} {n : ℕ} :
104	    Abelian.Ext.{w} X Y n ≃ₗ[R] Abelian.Ext.{w'} X Y n where
105	  toFun a := Abelian.Ext.chgUniv.{w'} a
106	  invFun a := Abelian.Ext.chgUniv.{w} a
107	  left_inv a := Abelian.Ext.chgUniv.{w'}.left_inv a
108	  right_inv a := Abelian.Ext.chgUniv.{w'}.right_inv a
109	  map_add' a b := Abelian.Ext.chgUniv_add a b
110	  map_smul' r a := Abelian.Ext.chgUniv_smul r a
111	
112	namespace AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme
113	
114	/-- Phase A step 6 *Path 2* (iter-016): the substantive functor mirroring
115	Mathlib's `Sheaf.cohomologyPresheafFunctor` for the `ModuleCat k` flavor. Sends
116	a sheaf `F : Sheaf J (ModuleCat k)` to the presheaf
117	`X ↦ Ext^n((presheafToSheaf J _).obj ((yoneda ⋙ ModuleCat.free k).obj X), F)`,
118	i.e.\ to a presheaf `Cᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat` whose value at `op X` is
119	`HModule' k F n X` (definitionally, see `HModule'_cohomologyPresheaf` below).
120	
121	The codomain is `Cᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat` (not `Cᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat k`) because Mathlib's
122	`Abelian.extFunctor n : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ C ⥤ AddCommGrpCat` always lands in `AddCommGrpCat`
123	regardless of the source category's `Linear`-enrichment; the per-fiber `Module k`
124	structure on `(HModule'_cohomologyPresheaf k F n).obj (op X)` is preserved
125	through the iter-014 `HModule'` reducibility chain. Probe-confirmed body
126	(iter-016 plan-agent). Used downstream as the prerequisite for the queued
127	iter-017+ `ModuleCat k`-flavored Mayer-Vietoris LES. -/
128	noncomputable def HModule'_cohomologyPresheafFunctor
129	    (k : Type u) [Field k]
130	    {C : Type v} [Category.{u, v} C] (J : GrothendieckTopology C)
131	    [HasWeakSheafify J (Type u)] [HasSheafify J (ModuleCat.{u} k)]
132	    [HasExt (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k))]
133	    (n : ℕ) :
134	    Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k) ⥤ Cᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat :=
135	  Functor.flip
136	    ((yoneda ⋙ (Functor.whiskeringRight _ _ _).obj (ModuleCat.free k) ⋙
137	      presheafToSheaf _ _).op ⋙ Abelian.extFunctor n)
138	
139	/-- Phase A step 6 *Path 2* (iter-016): the abbrev wrapper mirroring Mathlib's
140	`Sheaf.cohomologyPresheaf` for the `ModuleCat k` flavor. Evaluates the
141	`HModule'_cohomologyPresheafFunctor` at a sheaf `F`, giving a presheaf
142	`Cᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat` whose value at `op X` is `HModule' k F n X` definitionally
143	(probe-confirmed `rfl` by the iter-016 plan-agent). The `noncomputable abbrev`
144	form is required for the per-fiber definitional identification with `HModule'`;
145	under `def` the wrapper would block the `rfl`-level reduction that downstream
146	Mayer-Vietoris and Stein-factorization arguments rely on. -/
147	noncomputable abbrev HModule'_cohomologyPresheaf
148	    (k : Type u) [Field k]
149	    {C : Type v} [Category.{u, v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
150	    [HasWeakSheafify J (Type u)] [HasSheafify J (ModuleCat.{u} k)]
151	    [HasExt (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k))]
152	    (F : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k)) (n : ℕ) :
153	    Cᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat :=
154	  (HModule'_cohomologyPresheafFunctor k J n).obj F
155	
156	/-- Phase A step 6 *Path 2* (iter-017): the first Mayer-Vietoris LES building
157	block on the `ModuleCat k` side — the sum of the two restriction maps
158	`(cohomologyPresheaf F n).map S.f₂₄.op` and `(cohomologyPresheaf F n).map S.f₃₄.op`,
159	as a single map into the biproduct. Direct mirror of Mathlib's
160	`GrothendieckTopology.MayerVietorisSquare.toBiprod` (file
161	`Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Sites/SheafCohomology/MayerVietoris.lean`, L43–46) for
162	the `ModuleCat k` flavor with `F.cohomologyPresheaf → HModule'_cohomologyPresheaf k F`.
163	
164	The codomain `(... ).obj (op S.X₂) ⊞ (...).obj (op S.X₃)` is the biproduct in
165	`AddCommGrpCat` (Mathlib `Mathlib/Algebra/Category/Grp/Biproducts.lean`); since
166	`HModule'_cohomologyPresheaf k F n` is `Cᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat`, the biproduct
167	auto-resolves. Probe-confirmed body (iter-017 plan-agent). Used downstream as the
168	first of three Mayer-Vietoris LES building blocks; iter-018 will add the
169	composition-is-zero lemma and the connecting hom `δ`, iter-019 the LES sequence
170	and exactness theorem. -/
171	noncomputable def HModule'_toBiprod
172	    (k : Type u) [Field k]
173	    {C : Type v} [Category.{u, v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
174	    [HasWeakSheafify J (Type u)] [HasSheafify J (ModuleCat.{u} k)]
175	    [HasExt (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k))]
176	    (S : J.MayerVietorisSquare) (F : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k)) (n : ℕ) :
177	    (HModule'_cohomologyPresheaf k F n).obj (Opposite.op S.X₄) ⟶
178	      (HModule'_cohomologyPresheaf k F n).obj (Opposite.op S.X₂) ⊞
179	        (HModule'_cohomologyPresheaf k F n).obj (Opposite.op S.X₃) :=
180	  biprod.lift ((HModule'_cohomologyPresheaf k F n).map S.f₂₄.op)
181	              ((HModule'_cohomologyPresheaf k F n).map S.f₃₄.op)
182	
183	/-- Phase A step 6 *Path 2* (iter-017): the second Mayer-Vietoris LES building
184	block on the `ModuleCat k` side — the difference of the two restriction maps
185	`(cohomologyPresheaf F n).map S.f₁₂.op` and `(cohomologyPresheaf F n).map S.f₁₃.op`,
186	as a single map out of the biproduct. Direct mirror of Mathlib's
187	`GrothendieckTopology.MayerVietorisSquare.fromBiprod` (file
188	`Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Sites/SheafCohomology/MayerVietoris.lean`, L67–70) for
189	the `ModuleCat k` flavor.
190	
191	The negation `-(HModule'_cohomologyPresheaf k F n).map S.f₁₃.op` uses the
192	preadditive structure on `AddCommGrpCat`-morphisms; the sign is the standard
193	Mayer-Vietoris convention encoding the alternating-sum structure of the Čech
194	complex. Probe-confirmed body (iter-017 plan-agent). -/
195	noncomputable def HModule'_fromBiprod
196	    (k : Type u) [Field k]
197	    {C : Type v} [Category.{u, v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
198	    [HasWeakSheafify J (Type u)] [HasSheafify J (ModuleCat.{u} k)]
199	    [HasExt (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k))]
200	    (S : J.MayerVietorisSquare) (F : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k)) (n : ℕ) :
201	    (HModule'_cohomologyPresheaf k F n).obj (Opposite.op S.X₂) ⊞
202	        (HModule'_cohomologyPresheaf k F n).obj (Opposite.op S.X₃) ⟶
203	      (HModule'_cohomologyPresheaf k F n).obj (Opposite.op S.X₁) :=
204	  biprod.desc ((HModule'_cohomologyPresheaf k F n).map S.f₁₂.op)
205	              (-(HModule'_cohomologyPresheaf k F n).map S.f₁₃.op)
206	
207	/-- Phase A step 6 *Path 2* (iter-018): the third Mayer-Vietoris LES building
208	block on the `ModuleCat k` side — the composition-is-zero lemma asserting
209	`HModule'_toBiprod k S F n ≫ HModule'_fromBiprod k S F n = 0`. Direct mirror
210	of Mathlib's `GrothendieckTopology.MayerVietorisSquare.toBiprod_fromBiprod`
211	(file `Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Sites/SheafCohomology/MayerVietoris.lean`,
212	L72–75) for the `ModuleCat k` flavor.
213	
214	The proof unwinds via the biproduct universal property
215	(`biprod.lift_desc : biprod.lift a b ≫ biprod.desc c d = a ≫ c + b ≫ d`),
216	the preadditive negation (`Preadditive.comp_neg`), the addition-of-negation
217	arithmetic (`← sub_eq_add_neg`), the zero-iff-equal arithmetic
218	(`sub_eq_zero`), the contravariant functoriality of `cohomologyPresheaf`
219	(`← Functor.map_comp`, `← op_comp`), and the Mayer-Vietoris square
220	factorisation `S.toSquare.fac` (which says `S.f₁₂ ≫ S.f₂₄ = S.f₁₃ ≫ S.f₃₄`).
221	Probe-confirmed proof (iter-018 plan-agent); the `simp only` set transfers
222	verbatim from Mathlib's `AddCommGrpCat`-flavored proof because every step
223	is value-category-agnostic.
224	
225	The `@[reassoc (attr := simp)]` attribute generates the post-composition
226	form `… ≫ HModule'_fromBiprod … ≫ Z = 0 ≫ Z = 0` and registers the lemma
227	as a `simp` lemma; both are required for downstream Mayer-Vietoris LES
228	exactness arguments. -/
229	@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
230	lemma HModule'_toBiprod_fromBiprod
231	    (k : Type u) [Field k]
232	    {C : Type v} [Category.{u, v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
233	    [HasWeakSheafify J (Type u)] [HasSheafify J (ModuleCat.{u} k)]
234	    [HasExt (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k))]
235	    (S : J.MayerVietorisSquare) (F : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k)) (n : ℕ) :
236	    HModule'_toBiprod k S F n ≫ HModule'_fromBiprod k S F n = 0 := by
237	  simp only [HModule'_toBiprod, HModule'_fromBiprod, biprod.lift_desc,
238	    Preadditive.comp_neg, ← sub_eq_add_neg, sub_eq_zero,
239	    ← Functor.map_comp, ← op_comp, S.toSquare.fac]
240	
241	/-- Phase A step 6 *Path 2* (iter-019 helper, Mathlib gap-fill): `ModuleCat.free k`
242	is left adjoint to `forget (ModuleCat k)`. Mathlib's
243	`Mathlib/Algebra/Category/ModuleCat/Adjunctions.lean` provides the adjunction
244	`ModuleCat.adj k : ModuleCat.free k ⊣ forget (ModuleCat k)` but does not register
245	the corresponding `IsLeftAdjoint` instance (whereas `AddCommGrpCat.free.IsLeftAdjoint`
246	is registered in `Mathlib/Algebra/Category/Grp/Adjunctions.lean` L84). This
247	project-local instance fills the gap so that `Sheaf.composeAndSheafify J (ModuleCat.free k)`
248	acquires the necessary `PreservesColimit` instance, used by
249	`HModule'_isPushoutModuleCatFreeSheaf` below. -/
250	instance ModuleCat_free_isLeftAdjoint
251	    (k : Type u) [Field k] : (ModuleCat.free k).IsLeftAdjoint :=
252	  ⟨_, ⟨ModuleCat.adj k⟩⟩
253	
254	/-- Phase A step 6 *Path 2* (iter-019): the `ModuleCat k`-flavored
255	pushout-of-free-sheaves analog of Mathlib's
256	`GrothendieckTopology.MayerVietorisSquare.isPushoutAddCommGrpFreeSheaf`
257	(file `Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Sites/MayerVietorisSquare.lean`, L154–160).
258	States that the image of the Mayer-Vietoris square `S` under the composite
259	`yoneda ⋙ Functor.whiskeringRight ⋅ (ModuleCat.free k) ⋙ presheafToSheaf J _`
260	is a pushout square in `Sheaf J (ModuleCat k)`. The proof transfers the
261	type-level pushout `S.isPushout` through `Sheaf.composeAndSheafify J (ModuleCat.free k)`
262	(which preserves pushouts because `(ModuleCat.free k).IsLeftAdjoint`, registered
263	in `ModuleCat_free_isLeftAdjoint` above) and adjusts via the canonical iso
264	`presheafToSheafCompComposeAndSheafifyIso`.
265	
266	Probe-confirmed body (iter-019 plan-agent); the proof is verbatim from Mathlib L156–160
267	with `AddCommGrpCat.free → ModuleCat.free k`. Used downstream in iter-020+ to
268	prove `Mono` / `Epi` / `Exact` instances on the iter-019 short complex
269	`HModule'_shortComplex`, and ultimately in the iter-022+ `δ` connecting hom. -/
270	lemma HModule'_isPushoutModuleCatFreeSheaf
271	    (k : Type u) [Field k]
272	    {C : Type v} [Category.{u, v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
273	    [HasWeakSheafify J (Type u)] [HasSheafify J (ModuleCat.{u} k)]
274	    (S : J.MayerVietorisSquare) :
275	    (S.map (yoneda ⋙ (Functor.whiskeringRight _ _ _).obj (ModuleCat.free k) ⋙
276	      presheafToSheaf J _)).IsPushout :=
277	  (S.isPushout.map (Sheaf.composeAndSheafify J (ModuleCat.free k))).of_iso
278	    ((Square.mapFunctor.mapIso
279	      (presheafToSheafCompComposeAndSheafifyIso J (ModuleCat.free k))).app
280	        (S.map yoneda))
281	
282	/-- Phase A step 6 *Path 2* (iter-019): the `ModuleCat k`-flavored
283	short complex of free sheaves underlying the Mayer-Vietoris LES.
284	Direct mirror of Mathlib's `GrothendieckTopology.MayerVietorisSquare.shortComplex`
285	(file `Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Sites/MayerVietorisSquare.lean`, L234–249) for the
286	`ModuleCat k` flavor with `AddCommGrpCat.free → ModuleCat.free k`.
287	
288	The objects are the sheafified free `ModuleCat k`-valued presheaves on the four
289	vertices of the Mayer-Vietoris square (with the middle pair `S.X₂` and `S.X₃`
290	biproduct-summed). The two morphisms are: `f` (the difference `(yoneda.map S.f₁₂)
291	– (yoneda.map S.f₁₃)` lifted through the biproduct), and `g` (the sum
292	`(yoneda.map S.f₂₄) + (yoneda.map S.f₃₄)` desced through the biproduct).
293	The `zero` proof (i.e.\ `f ≫ g = 0`) follows from the
294	`cokernelCofork.condition` of the pushout square in
295	`HModule'_isPushoutModuleCatFreeSheaf` above.
296	
297	Probe-confirmed body (iter-019 plan-agent); structure-literal mirror of Mathlib L235–249
298	with `AddCommGrpCat.free → ModuleCat.free k`. The `@[simps]` attribute generates
299	field-projection simp lemmas (`HModule'_shortComplex_X₁`, `..._X₂`, `..._X₃`,
300	`..._f`, `..._g`) consumed by the iter-020+ `Mono`/`Epi`/`Exact`/`ShortExact`
301	proofs and the iter-022+ `δ` definition. -/
302	@[simps]
303	noncomputable def HModule'_shortComplex
304	    (k : Type u) [Field k]
305	    {C : Type v} [Category.{u, v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
306	    [HasWeakSheafify J (Type u)] [HasSheafify J (ModuleCat.{u} k)]
307	    (S : J.MayerVietorisSquare) :
308	    ShortComplex (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k)) where
309	  X₁ := (presheafToSheaf J _).obj (yoneda.obj S.X₁ ⋙ ModuleCat.free k)
310	  X₂ := (presheafToSheaf J _).obj (yoneda.obj S.X₂ ⋙ ModuleCat.free k) ⊞
311	    (presheafToSheaf J _).obj (yoneda.obj S.X₃ ⋙ ModuleCat.free k)
312	  X₃ := (presheafToSheaf J _).obj (yoneda.obj S.X₄ ⋙ ModuleCat.free k)
313	  f :=
314	    biprod.lift
315	      ((presheafToSheaf J _).map (Functor.whiskerRight (yoneda.map S.f₁₂) _))
316	      (-(presheafToSheaf J _).map (Functor.whiskerRight (yoneda.map S.f₁₃) _))
317	  g :=
318	    biprod.desc
319	      ((presheafToSheaf J _).map (Functor.whiskerRight (yoneda.map S.f₂₄) _))
320	      ((presheafToSheaf J _).map (Functor.whiskerRight (yoneda.map S.f₃₄) _))
321	  zero :=
322	    (S.map (yoneda ⋙ (Functor.whiskeringRight _ _ _).obj (ModuleCat.free k) ⋙
323	        presheafToSheaf J _)).cokernelCofork.condition
324	
325	/-- Phase A step 6 *Path 2* (iter-020 helper, Mathlib gap-fill): the free-module
326	functor `ModuleCat.free k : Type u ⥤ ModuleCat.{u} k` preserves monomorphisms.
327	Mathlib registers `AddCommGrpCat.instPreservesMonomorphismsFree :
328	AddCommGrpCat.free.PreservesMonomorphisms` in
329	`Mathlib/Algebra/Category/Grp/Adjunctions.lean` but does not register the
330	corresponding instance for `ModuleCat.free k` in
331	`Mathlib/Algebra/Category/ModuleCat/Adjunctions.lean`. This project-local
332	instance fills the gap so that, after `simp only [biprod.lift_snd]`, the
333	typeclass-search engine can discharge the residual `Mono` goal in the proof
334	of `HModule'_shortComplex_f_mono` below.
335	
336	The proof: for an injective function `f : X → Y` between types,
337	`(ModuleCat.free k).map f = ModuleCat.ofHom (Finsupp.lmapDomain k k f)` (defeq),
338	and `Finsupp.mapDomain f` is injective on `Finsupp X k → Finsupp Y k` by
339	Mathlib's `Finsupp.mapDomain_injective`. Bridging via `ModuleCat.mono_iff_injective`
340	recovers `Mono` in `ModuleCat k`. -/
341	instance ModuleCat_free_preservesMonomorphisms
342	    (k : Type u) [Field k] : (ModuleCat.free k).PreservesMonomorphisms := by
343	  refine ⟨fun {X Y} f hf ↦ ?_⟩
344	  have hf' : Function.Injective f := (CategoryTheory.mono_iff_injective f).mp hf
345	  rw [ModuleCat.mono_iff_injective]
346	  exact Finsupp.mapDomain_injective hf'

353	-- form of `(HModule'_shortComplex k S).f` past structure-literal projection.
354	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
355	instance HModule'_shortComplex_f_mono
356	    (k : Type u) [Field k]

359	    (S : J.MayerVietorisSquare) :

361	  have : Mono ((HModule'_shortComplex k S).f ≫ biprod.snd) := by
362	    simp only [HModule'_shortComplex_f, biprod.lift_snd]
363	    infer_instance

367	epimorphism in `Sheaf J (ModuleCat k)`. Direct mirror of Mathlib's
368	`MayerVietorisSquare.lean` L259–261 with `AddCommGrpCat.free → ModuleCat.free k`.

370	`ShortComplex.exact_and_epi_g_iff_g_is_cokernel` and the iter-019 lemma
371	`HModule'_isPushoutModuleCatFreeSheaf`'s `isColimitCokernelCofork` accessor. -/

376	    (S : J.MayerVietorisSquare) :
377	    Epi (HModule'_shortComplex k S).g :=
378	  ((HModule'_shortComplex k S).exact_and_epi_g_iff_g_is_cokernel.2
379	    ⟨(HModule'_isPushoutModuleCatFreeSheaf k S).isColimitCokernelCofork⟩).2

381	/-- Phase A step 6 *Path 2* (iter-020): `(HModule'_shortComplex k S).Exact`,
382	i.e. the kernel of `g` equals the image of `f` in `Sheaf J (ModuleCat k)`.
383	Direct mirror of Mathlib's `MayerVietorisSquare.lean` L263–265 with
384	`AddCommGrpCat.free → ModuleCat.free k`. The proof is a one-line term-mode
385	body using `ShortComplex.exact_of_g_is_cokernel` and the iter-019 lemma

387	lemma HModule'_shortComplex_exact
388	    (k : Type u) [Field k]
389	    {C : Type v} [Category.{u, v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}

391	    (S : J.MayerVietorisSquare) :
392	    (HModule'_shortComplex k S).Exact :=
393	  ShortComplex.exact_of_g_is_cokernel _
394	    (HModule'_isPushoutModuleCatFreeSheaf k S).isColimitCokernelCofork

396	/-- Phase A step 6 *Path 2* (iter-020): `(HModule'_shortComplex k S).ShortExact`,
397	the short-exact predicate (combining `Mono f`, `Epi g`, and `Exact`) in
398	`Sheaf J (ModuleCat k)`. Direct mirror of Mathlib's `MayerVietorisSquare.lean`
399	L267–268 with `AddCommGrpCat.free → ModuleCat.free k`. The proof is a one-line
400	anonymous-constructor: the `Mono f` and `Epi g` predicates are typeclass-resolved
401	from `HModule'_shortComplex_f_mono` and `HModule'_shortComplex_g_epi`, leaving
402	only the `exact` field which is filled with `HModule'_shortComplex_exact`. The
403	named lemma is consumed in iter-021+ as `S.HModule'_shortComplex_shortExact.extClass`
404	to define the connecting hom `HModule'_δ` of the Mayer-Vietoris LES. -/
405	lemma HModule'_shortComplex_shortExact
406	    (k : Type u) [Field k]
407	    {C : Type v} [Category.{u, v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
408	    [HasWeakSheafify J (Type u)] [HasSheafify J (ModuleCat.{u} k)]
409	    (S : J.MayerVietorisSquare) :
410	    (HModule'_shortComplex k S).ShortExact where
411	  exact := HModule'_shortComplex_exact k S

413	/-- Phase A step 6 *Path 2* (iter-021): the connecting homomorphism `δ` of the
414	Mayer-Vietoris long exact sequence in `ModuleCat k`-valued sheaf cohomology.
415	For a Mayer-Vietoris square `S` and adjacent cohomological degrees `n₀ + 1 = n₁`,
416	the morphism
417	  δ : (HModule'_cohomologyPresheaf k F n₀).obj (op S.X₁) ⟶
418	        (HModule'_cohomologyPresheaf k F n₁).obj (op S.X₄)
419	in `AddCommGrpCat` is the precomposition with the extension class
420	`(HModule'_shortComplex_shortExact k S).extClass : Ext (...X₁...) (...X₃...) 1`
421	followed by `AddCommGrpCat.ofHom` to wrap the resulting `AddMonoidHom` as a
422	categorical morphism. Direct mirror of Mathlib's `MayerVietorisSquare.δ`
423	(`Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Sites/SheafCohomology/MayerVietoris.lean` L112–114)
424	for the `ModuleCat k` flavor with `AddCommGrpCat.free → ModuleCat.free k`.
425	
426	The `[HasExt (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k))]` typeclass is required (the
427	`Ext.precomp` operation depends on it) and matches the corresponding
428	requirement on iter-016 `HModule'_cohomologyPresheafFunctor` / `..._cohomologyPresheaf`,
429	iter-017 `HModule'_toBiprod` / `..._fromBiprod`, and iter-018
430	`HModule'_toBiprod_fromBiprod`.
431	
432	This connecting hom is the missing third link of the Mayer-Vietoris exact
433	sequence: combined with iter-017's `toBiprod` (sum of restriction) and
434	`fromBiprod` (difference of restriction), iter-018's `toBiprod ≫ fromBiprod = 0`,
435	and the iter-022+ packaging into a `ComposableArrows`-form sequence + iter-023+
436	sequence-iso to `Ext.contravariantSequence` + iter-024+ exactness theorem, it
437	will yield the full LES `... → Hⁿ(X₄) → Hⁿ(X₂) ⊞ Hⁿ(X₃) → Hⁿ(X₁) → Hⁿ⁺¹(X₄) → ...`
438	in `ModuleCat k`-valued sheaf cohomology. -/
439	noncomputable def HModule'_δ
440	    (k : Type u) [Field k]
441	    {C : Type v} [Category.{u, v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
442	    [HasWeakSheafify J (Type u)] [HasSheafify J (ModuleCat.{u} k)]
443	    [HasExt (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k))]
444	    (S : J.MayerVietorisSquare) (F : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k))
445	    (n₀ n₁ : ℕ) (h : n₀ + 1 = n₁) :
446	    (HModule'_cohomologyPresheaf k F n₀).obj (Opposite.op S.X₁) ⟶
447	      (HModule'_cohomologyPresheaf k F n₁).obj (Opposite.op S.X₄) :=
448	  AddCommGrpCat.ofHom ((HModule'_shortComplex_shortExact k S).extClass.precomp _ (by omega))
449	
450	/-- Phase A step 6 *Path 2* (iter-022): the Mayer-Vietoris long exact sequence
451	in `ModuleCat k`-valued sheaf cohomology, packaged as a `ComposableArrows` of
452	length 5 in `AddCommGrpCat`. The five composable morphisms are, in order,
453	`HModule'_toBiprod` at degree `n₀`, `HModule'_fromBiprod` at degree `n₀`, the
454	connecting hom `HModule'_δ` from degree `n₀` to degree `n₁`, `HModule'_toBiprod`
455	at degree `n₁`, and `HModule'_fromBiprod` at degree `n₁`. Direct mirror of
456	Mathlib's `MayerVietorisSquare.sequence`
457	(`Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Sites/SheafCohomology/MayerVietoris.lean` L120–122)
458	for the `ModuleCat k` flavor.
459	
460	The `noncomputable abbrev` form is load-bearing: downstream `dsimp`-based
461	unfolding (in iter-023+ `HModule'_sequenceIso` and iter-024+
462	`HModule'_sequence_exact`) needs to access `mk₅`'s field-projection simp
463	lemmas through the abbrev. -/
464	noncomputable abbrev HModule'_sequence
465	    (k : Type u) [Field k]
466	    {C : Type v} [Category.{u, v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
467	    [HasWeakSheafify J (Type u)] [HasSheafify J (ModuleCat.{u} k)]
468	    [HasExt (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k))]
469	    (S : J.MayerVietorisSquare) (F : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k))
470	    (n₀ n₁ : ℕ) (h : n₀ + 1 = n₁) :
471	    ComposableArrows AddCommGrpCat 5 :=
472	  ComposableArrows.mk₅ (HModule'_toBiprod k S F n₀) (HModule'_fromBiprod k S F n₀)
473	    (HModule'_δ k S F n₀ n₁ h)
474	    (HModule'_toBiprod k S F n₁) (HModule'_fromBiprod k S F n₁)
475	
476	/-- Iter-023 aux lemma 1: explicit elementwise formula for `HModule'_toBiprod`
477	(mirror Mathlib `MayerVietoris.lean` L48–64). -/
478	lemma HModule'_toBiprod_apply
479	    (k : Type u) [Field k]
480	    {C : Type v} [Category.{u, v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
481	    [HasWeakSheafify J (Type u)] [HasSheafify J (ModuleCat.{u} k)]
482	    [HasExt (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k))]
483	    (S : J.MayerVietorisSquare) (F : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k))
484	    {n : ℕ} (y : (HModule'_cohomologyPresheaf k F n).obj (Opposite.op S.X₄)) :
485	    HModule'_toBiprod k S F n y =
486	      (AddCommGrpCat.biprodIsoProd _ _).inv
487	        ⟨(HModule'_cohomologyPresheaf k F n).map S.f₂₄.op y,
488	          (HModule'_cohomologyPresheaf k F n).map S.f₃₄.op y⟩ := by
489	  apply (AddCommGrpCat.biprodIsoProd _ _).addCommGroupIsoToAddEquiv.injective
490	  dsimp [HModule'_toBiprod]
491	  ext
492	  · rw [Iso.addCommGroupIsoToAddEquiv_apply, Iso.addCommGroupIsoToAddEquiv_apply,
493	      ← AddCommGrpCat.biprodIsoProd_inv_comp_fst_apply, Iso.hom_inv_id_apply,
494	      ← ConcreteCategory.comp_apply, biprod.lift_fst, Iso.inv_hom_id_apply]
495	  · rw [Iso.addCommGroupIsoToAddEquiv_apply, Iso.addCommGroupIsoToAddEquiv_apply,
496	      ← AddCommGrpCat.biprodIsoProd_inv_comp_snd_apply, Iso.hom_inv_id_apply,
497	      ← ConcreteCategory.comp_apply, biprod.lift_snd, Iso.inv_hom_id_apply]
498	
499	/-- Iter-023 aux lemma 2: explicit elementwise formula for `HModule'_fromBiprod`
500	on the inverse of `biprodIsoProd` (mirror Mathlib L77–83). -/
501	lemma HModule'_fromBiprod_biprodIsoProd_inv_apply
502	    (k : Type u) [Field k]
503	    {C : Type v} [Category.{u, v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
504	    [HasWeakSheafify J (Type u)] [HasSheafify J (ModuleCat.{u} k)]
505	    [HasExt (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k))]
506	    (S : J.MayerVietorisSquare) (F : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k))
507	    {n : ℕ}
508	    (y₁ : (HModule'_cohomologyPresheaf k F n).obj (Opposite.op S.X₂))
509	    (y₂ : (HModule'_cohomologyPresheaf k F n).obj (Opposite.op S.X₃)) :
510	    HModule'_fromBiprod k S F n
511	        ((AddCommGrpCat.biprodIsoProd _ _).inv ⟨y₁, y₂⟩) =
512	      (HModule'_cohomologyPresheaf k F n).map S.f₁₂.op y₁ -
513	        (HModule'_cohomologyPresheaf k F n).map S.f₁₃.op y₂ := by
514	  dsimp [HModule'_fromBiprod]
515	  rw [← ConcreteCategory.comp_apply]
516	  simp [AddCommGrpCat.biprodIsoProd_inv_comp_desc, sub_eq_add_neg]
517	
518	-- Iter-023 aux lemma 3: bridges `AddCommGrpCat`-side `biprodIsoProd` and
519	-- `Ext`-side `Ext.biprodAddEquiv` for the `toBiprod` morphism
520	-- (mirror Mathlib L85–91). The `set_option ... in` and `attribute ... in`
521	-- wrappers match Mathlib L85, L86 verbatim.
522	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
523	attribute [local simp] HModule'_toBiprod_apply in
524	lemma HModule'_biprodAddEquiv_symm_biprodIsoProd_hom_toBiprod_apply
525	    (k : Type u) [Field k]
526	    {C : Type v} [Category.{u, v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
527	    [HasWeakSheafify J (Type u)] [HasSheafify J (ModuleCat.{u} k)]
528	    [HasExt (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k))]
529	    (S : J.MayerVietorisSquare) (F : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k))
530	    {n : ℕ} (x : (HModule'_cohomologyPresheaf k F n).obj (Opposite.op S.X₄)) :
531	    Abelian.Ext.biprodAddEquiv.symm
532	        ((AddCommGrpCat.biprodIsoProd _ _).hom (HModule'_toBiprod k S F n x)) =
533	      (Abelian.Ext.mk₀ (HModule'_shortComplex k S).g).comp x (zero_add n) :=
534	  Abelian.Ext.biprodAddEquiv.injective (by cat_disch)
535	
536	-- Iter-023 aux lemma 4: bridges the same machinery for the `fromBiprod`
537	-- morphism (mirror Mathlib L93–106).
538	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
539	attribute [local simp] sub_eq_add_neg in
540	lemma HModule'_mk₀_f_comp_biprodAddEquiv_symm_biprodIsoProd_hom
541	    (k : Type u) [Field k]
542	    {C : Type v} [Category.{u, v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
543	    [HasWeakSheafify J (Type u)] [HasSheafify J (ModuleCat.{u} k)]
544	    [HasExt (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k))]
545	    (S : J.MayerVietorisSquare) (F : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k))
546	    {n : ℕ}
547	    (x : ↑((HModule'_cohomologyPresheaf k F n).obj (Opposite.op S.X₂) ⊞
548	           (HModule'_cohomologyPresheaf k F n).obj (Opposite.op S.X₃))) :
549	    (Abelian.Ext.mk₀ (HModule'_shortComplex k S).f).comp
550	        (Abelian.Ext.biprodAddEquiv.symm
551	          ((AddCommGrpCat.biprodIsoProd _ _).hom x)) (zero_add n) =
552	      (HModule'_fromBiprod k S F n x) := by
553	  obtain ⟨⟨x₂, x₃⟩, rfl⟩ :=
554	    (AddCommGrpCat.biprodIsoProd _ _).addCommGroupIsoToAddEquiv.symm.surjective x
555	  dsimp
556	  rw [Abelian.Ext.biprodAddEquiv_symm_apply,
557	    Iso.addCommGroupIsoToAddEquiv_symm_apply,
558	    HModule'_fromBiprod_biprodIsoProd_inv_apply]
559	  cat_disch
560	
561	-- Iter-023 main: comparison iso from the iter-022 LES sequence to
562	-- `Ext.contravariantSequence` (mirror Mathlib L124–138). The technical heart
563	-- of the Mayer-Vietoris LES.
564	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
565	noncomputable def HModule'_sequenceIso
566	    (k : Type u) [Field k]
567	    {C : Type v} [Category.{u, v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
568	    [HasWeakSheafify J (Type u)] [HasSheafify J (ModuleCat.{u} k)]
569	    [HasExt (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k))]
570	    (S : J.MayerVietorisSquare) (F : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k))
571	    (n₀ n₁ : ℕ) (h : n₀ + 1 = n₁) :
572	    HModule'_sequence k S F n₀ n₁ h ≅
573	      Abelian.Ext.contravariantSequence (HModule'_shortComplex_shortExact k S)
574	        F n₀ n₁ (by omega) :=
575	  ComposableArrows.isoMk₅ (Iso.refl _)
576	    ((AddCommGrpCat.biprodIsoProd _ _).trans
577	      (Abelian.Ext.biprodAddEquiv.symm).toAddCommGrpIso)
578	    (Iso.refl _) (Iso.refl _)
579	    ((AddCommGrpCat.biprodIsoProd _ _).trans
580	      (Abelian.Ext.biprodAddEquiv.symm).toAddCommGrpIso)
581	    (Iso.refl _)
582	    (by ext; apply HModule'_biprodAddEquiv_symm_biprodIsoProd_hom_toBiprod_apply)
583	    (by ext; symm; apply HModule'_mk₀_f_comp_biprodAddEquiv_symm_biprodIsoProd_hom)
584	    (by simp [ComposableArrows.Precomp.map]; rfl)
585	    (by ext; apply HModule'_biprodAddEquiv_symm_biprodIsoProd_hom_toBiprod_apply)
586	    (by ext; symm; apply HModule'_mk₀_f_comp_biprodAddEquiv_symm_biprodIsoProd_hom)
587	
588	/-- Iter-026: Mayer-Vietoris LES exactness theorem (mirror Mathlib
589	`MayerVietoris.lean` L140–141). The iter-022 sequence is exact via the iter-023
590	comparison iso to `Ext.contravariantSequence`. -/
591	lemma HModule'_sequence_exact
592	    (k : Type u) [Field k]
593	    {C : Type v} [Category.{u, v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
594	    [HasWeakSheafify J (Type u)] [HasSheafify J (ModuleCat.{u} k)]
595	    [HasExt (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k))]
596	    (S : J.MayerVietorisSquare) (F : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k))
597	    (n₀ n₁ : ℕ) (h : n₀ + 1 = n₁) :
598	    (HModule'_sequence k S F n₀ n₁ h).Exact :=
599	  ComposableArrows.exact_of_iso (HModule'_sequenceIso k S F n₀ n₁ h).symm
600	    (Abelian.Ext.contravariantSequence_exact _ _ _ _ _)
601	
602	/-- Iter-026: `δ ≫ toBiprod = 0` simp companion (mirror Mathlib L143–145). -/
603	@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
604	lemma HModule'_δ_toBiprod
605	    (k : Type u) [Field k]
606	    {C : Type v} [Category.{u, v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
607	    [HasWeakSheafify J (Type u)] [HasSheafify J (ModuleCat.{u} k)]
608	    [HasExt (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k))]
609	    (S : J.MayerVietorisSquare) (F : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k))
610	    (n₀ n₁ : ℕ) (h : n₀ + 1 = n₁) :
611	    HModule'_δ k S F n₀ n₁ h ≫ HModule'_toBiprod k S F n₁ = 0 :=
612	  (HModule'_sequence_exact k S F n₀ n₁ h).zero 2
613	
614	/-- Iter-026: `fromBiprod ≫ δ = 0` simp companion (mirror Mathlib L147–149). -/
615	@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
616	lemma HModule'_fromBiprod_δ
617	    (k : Type u) [Field k]
618	    {C : Type v} [Category.{u, v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
619	    [HasWeakSheafify J (Type u)] [HasSheafify J (ModuleCat.{u} k)]
620	    [HasExt (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k))]
621	    (S : J.MayerVietorisSquare) (F : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k))
622	    (n₀ n₁ : ℕ) (h : n₀ + 1 = n₁) :
623	    HModule'_fromBiprod k S F n₀ ≫ HModule'_δ k S F n₀ n₁ h = 0 :=
624	  (HModule'_sequence_exact k S F n₀ n₁ h).zero 1
625

39	/-- Phase A step 6 *Path 2* (iter-028): a bundled 2-affine cover of a scheme
40	together with the affineness of the pairwise intersection. The geometric input
41	to the abstract Mayer-Vietoris LES `HModule'_sequence_exact` consumes — packaged
42	to record the affineness conditions and the cover-totality hypothesis that the
43	abstract MV-square does not capture. The accessor `toMayerVietorisSquare`
44	produces the underlying Mathlib `MayerVietorisSquare`.
45	
46	Mathematically: a 2-affine open cover of `X` whose pairwise intersection is also
47	affine. The cover hypothesis `cover : U₁ ⊔ U₂ = ⊤` is load-bearing for downstream
48	Serre-finiteness use (it identifies the `MayerVietorisSquare` corner `X₄` with
49	the whole scheme `X`). -/
50	structure AffineCoverMVSquare (X : Scheme.{u}) where
51	  /-- First affine open of the cover. -/
52	  U₁ : X.Opens
53	  /-- Second affine open of the cover. -/
54	  U₂ : X.Opens
55	  /-- `U₁` is affine. -/
56	  isAffineOpen_U₁ : IsAffineOpen U₁
57	  /-- `U₂` is affine. -/

155	/-- Iter-031 cover-totality source-object identification. For a category `C`
156	with terminal object `T`, the sheafification of the free `k`-module on the
157	representable presheaf at `T` is canonically isomorphic to the constant sheaf
158	at `ModuleCat.of k k`. This is the natural-iso prerequisite for identifying
159	`HModule' k F n T` (open-evaluation cohomology at the terminal `T`, iter-014)
160	with `HModule k F n` (global cohomology, iter-009): both are `Ext` groups
161	whose source objects are made canonically isomorphic by this iso.
162	
163	Assembled from three Mathlib pieces, mirroring the structure
164	`constantSheaf J D = Functor.const Cᵒᵖ ⋙ presheafToSheaf J D`:
165	1. `yoneda.obj T ≅ (Functor.const Cᵒᵖ).obj PUnit` — the terminal-collapse
166	   of the representable, by `IsTerminal.from`/`IsTerminal.hom_ext`.
167	2. `Functor.constComp _ PUnit (ModuleCat.free k)` — the identity
168	   `(Functor.const Cᵒᵖ).obj PUnit ⋙ ModuleCat.free k =
169	    (Functor.const Cᵒᵖ).obj ((ModuleCat.free k).obj PUnit)`
170	   packaged as an iso.
171	3. `(Finsupp.LinearEquiv.finsuppUnique k k PUnit).toModuleIso` —
172	   `(ModuleCat.free k).obj PUnit ≅ ModuleCat.of k k`. -/
173	noncomputable def HModule'_top_sourceIso
174	    (k : Type u) [Field k]
175	    {C : Type v} [Category.{u, v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
176	    [HasWeakSheafify J (Type u)] [HasSheafify J (ModuleCat.{u} k)]
177	    {T : C} (hT : IsTerminal T) :
178	    (presheafToSheaf J _).obj
179	        ((yoneda ⋙ (Functor.whiskeringRight _ _ _).obj (ModuleCat.free k)).obj T)
180	      ≅ (constantSheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k)).obj (ModuleCat.of k k) :=
181	  (presheafToSheaf J _).mapIso
182	    (Functor.isoWhiskerRight
183	        (NatIso.ofComponents
184	          (fun _ => Equiv.toIso { toFun := fun _ => PUnit.unit
185	                                  invFun := fun _ => hT.from _
186	                                  left_inv := fun _ => hT.hom_ext _ _
187	                                  right_inv := fun _ => rfl })
188	          (fun _ => by ext; rfl))
189	        (ModuleCat.free k) ≪≫
190	      Functor.constComp _ PUnit.{u+1} (ModuleCat.free k) ≪≫
191	      (Functor.const Cᵒᵖ).mapIso
192	        (Finsupp.LinearEquiv.finsuppUnique k k PUnit).toModuleIso)

194	/-- Iter-032 cover-totality Ext-transport at universe `u+1`. Combining the
195	iter-031 `HModule'_top_sourceIso` (a sheaf-level natural iso between source
196	objects of two `Ext` computations) with the Mathlib Ext-API operation
197	`precompOfLinear` (pre-composition of `Ext` along an `Ext 0`-element) yields
198	a `k`-linear equivalence between the universe-`u+1` Ext at the sheafified
199	representable on `T` and `HModule k F n`.
200	
201	The universe annotation `Abelian.Ext.{u+1}` on the LHS is load-bearing —
202	without it Lean would pick `Ext.{u}` (matching iter-014's `HModule'` choice),
203	and the equivalence would not typecheck against `HModule k F n : Type (u+1)`
204	(iter-009). By pinning the LHS to `Ext.{u+1}` we sidestep the iter-031
205	universe mismatch (`HModule' : Type u` vs `HModule : Type (u+1)`); both
206	sides of this equivalence live at `Type (u+1)`. The bridge from
207	`HModule' k F n T : Type u` to the LHS here is iter-033+ work — most
208	plausibly via a small refactor on iter-014 to align `HModule'`'s universe,
209	or via a `ULift.{u+1}` wrapper.
210	
211	Body uses `LinearEquiv.ofLinear` with two pre-composition maps via the
212	iter-031 iso's hom/inv. The round-trip equations close by a four-step
213	rewrite: associativity (with the middle factor degree 0), composition
214	collapse via `mk₀_comp_mk₀`, the iso identity, and `mk₀_id_comp`. -/
215	noncomputable def HModule_top_linearEquiv
216	    (k : Type u) [Field k]
217	    {C : Type v} [Category.{u, v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
218	    [HasWeakSheafify J (Type u)] [HasSheafify J (ModuleCat.{u} k)]
219	    [HasExt (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k))]
220	    (F : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k)) (n : ℕ) {T : C} (hT : IsTerminal T) :
221	    Abelian.Ext.{u+1}
222	        ((presheafToSheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k)).obj
223	          ((yoneda ⋙ (Functor.whiskeringRight _ _ _).obj (ModuleCat.free k)).obj T)) F n
224	      ≃ₗ[k] HModule k F n :=
225	  let α := HModule'_top_sourceIso k hT
226	  LinearEquiv.ofLinear
227	    ((Abelian.Ext.mk₀ α.inv).precompOfLinear k F (zero_add n))
228	    ((Abelian.Ext.mk₀ α.hom).precompOfLinear k F (zero_add n))
229	    (by
230	      ext x
231	      change (Abelian.Ext.mk₀ α.inv).comp
232	        ((Abelian.Ext.mk₀ α.hom).comp x (zero_add n)) (zero_add n) = x
233	      rw [← Abelian.Ext.comp_assoc_of_second_deg_zero, Abelian.Ext.mk₀_comp_mk₀,
234	          α.inv_hom_id, Abelian.Ext.mk₀_id_comp])
235	    (by
236	      ext y
237	      change (Abelian.Ext.mk₀ α.hom).comp
238	        ((Abelian.Ext.mk₀ α.inv).comp y (zero_add n)) (zero_add n) = y
239	      rw [← Abelian.Ext.comp_assoc_of_second_deg_zero, Abelian.Ext.mk₀_comp_mk₀,
240	          α.hom_inv_id, Abelian.Ext.mk₀_id_comp])

8	/-!
9	# Sheaves of `k`-modules: finite-length carriers and producer instances
10	
11	Sub-file (3/3) of the `StructureSheafModuleK` split (refactor iter-174). This file
12	hosts the downstream finite-length carriers (`IsAffineHModuleVanishing`,
13	`IsHModuleHomFinite`), their algebraic bridges (the `HModule` / `HModule'`
14	abbrevs, the H⁰ `LinearEquiv` transport companions, the constant-sheaf-Γ adjunction
15	upgrade), and the curve-side producer instances. Upstream sub-files
16	`Presheaf.lean` and `SheafProperty.lean` provide the structure-sheaf object the
17	carriers depend on.
18	
19	Downstream finite-length carriers in this file:
20	
21	* H>0 affine cohomology vanishing is carried by iter-040's
22	  `IsAffineHModuleVanishing` (the producer instance for the curve case
23	  lives at iter-051).
24	* H⁰ Hom-finiteness is carried by iter-043's **wholespace**
25	  `IsHModuleHomFinite`; the producer instance on a proper geometrically
26	  integral $k$-curve is supplied at iter-046 from Stein finiteness
27	  (`module_finite_globalSections_of_isProper`).
28	* The iter-041 per-affine-open variant `IsAffineHModuleHomFinite` was an
29	  abandoned attempt (dead scaffolding — $\Gamma(U, O_C)$ is not finite
30	  over $k$ on a proper affine open of a non-trivial curve) and has been
31	  removed from this file.
32	
33	See `blueprint/src/chapters/Cohomology_StructureSheafModuleK.tex`.
34	-/
35	
36	set_option autoImplicit false
37	
38	universe u v
39	
40	open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace AlgebraicGeometry
41	
42	namespace AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme
43	
44	/-- Phase A step 5/6 bridge (iter-009 scaffold): the parallel `Sheaf.H` for
45	`ModuleCat k`-valued sheaves. Mathlib's `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.H` is
46	parameterised over `Sheaf J AddCommGrpCat` only, so closing `genus` honestly
47	requires this `ModuleCat k`-flavoured version. The result carries `Module k`
48	automatically via `CategoryTheory.Abelian.Ext.instModule`, and
49	`Module.finrank k` is therefore well-defined on it. The declaration is a
50	`noncomputable abbrev` (rather than `def`) so that instance synthesis sees
51	through the wrapper to find `Module k` and `AddCommGroup` instances. -/
52	noncomputable abbrev HModule
53	    (k : Type u) [Field k]
54	    {C : Type v} [Category.{u, v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
55	    [HasSheafify J (ModuleCat.{u} k)] [HasExt (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k))]
56	    (F : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k)) (n : ℕ) : Type (u+1) :=
57	  Abelian.Ext ((constantSheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k)).obj (ModuleCat.of k k)) F n
58	
59	/-- Phase A step 6 algebraic bridge (iter-010 scaffold): the $k$-linear
60	identification of `HModule k F 0` with the Hom group from the constant
61	sheaf at `ModuleCat.of k k`. Mathlib provides
62	`CategoryTheory.Abelian.Ext.linearEquiv₀ : Ext X Y 0 ≃ₗ[R] (X ⟶ Y)` in any
63	`Linear R`-enriched abelian category; specialised to the `Linear k`
64	enrichment of `Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k)` (auto-inferable from
65	`HasSheafify J (ModuleCat.{u} k)`), this collapses `HModule k F 0` to a
66	`k`-linear Hom group. The closure body is `Abelian.Ext.linearEquiv₀`;
67	probe-confirmed one-liner (iter-010 plan-agent). Used downstream to
68	identify `H⁰(C, toModuleKSheaf C)` with `Γ(C, O_C)` viewed as a
69	`k`-module on a connected proper `k`-curve. -/
70	noncomputable def HModule_zero_linearEquiv
71	    (k : Type u) [Field k]
72	    {C : Type v} [Category.{u, v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
73	    [HasSheafify J (ModuleCat.{u} k)] [HasExt (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k))]
74	    (F : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k)) :
75	    HModule k F 0 ≃ₗ[k]
76	      ((constantSheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k)).obj (ModuleCat.of k k) ⟶ F) :=
77	  Abelian.Ext.linearEquiv₀
78	
79	/-- Phase A step 6 *Path 2* (iter-013 scaffold): the `ModuleCat k`-flavored
80	cohomology of an open `X : C` with values in a sheaf `F : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k)`.
81	Mirrors Mathlib's `Sheaf.H' F n X = (F.cohomologyPresheaf n).obj (op X)`
82	(`Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Sites/SheafCohomology/Basic.lean` L105) for
83	`AddCommGrpCat`-valued sheaves, with `AddCommGrpCat.free → ModuleCat.free k`.
84	
85	The codomain is `Type u` (not `ModuleCat.{u} k`): `Abelian.Ext` returns a bare
86	`Type u` carrying `Module k` via `Abelian.Ext.instModule` through the `Linear k`
87	enrichment. The `noncomputable abbrev` form (rather than `def`) is required so
88	instance synthesis sees through the wrapper to find `Module k (HModule' k F n X)`
89	and `AddCommGroup (HModule' k F n X)` — under `def`, `Module.finrank` would fail
90	to typecheck (cf. iter-009 design rationale on `HModule`).
91	
92	This is the prerequisite for the iter-014+ `ModuleCat k`-flavored Mayer-Vietoris
93	LES (mirror of `Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Sites/SheafCohomology/MayerVietoris.lean`).
94	The iter-014+ work will state and prove the LES on a `MayerVietorisSquare`,
95	specialising to a 2-affine cover of a proper `k`-curve in iter-015+. The
96	comparison theorem `cechCohomology_OC C 𝒰 n ≅ HModule k (toModuleKSheaf C) n`
97	for an acyclic cover (the technical heart of Path-2) is also queued for
98	iter-015+. -/
99	noncomputable abbrev HModule' (k : Type u) [Field k]
100	    {C : Type v} [Category.{u, v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
101	    [HasWeakSheafify J (Type u)] [HasSheafify J (ModuleCat.{u} k)]
102	    [HasExt (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k))]
103	    (F : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k)) (n : ℕ) (X : C) : Type u :=
104	  Abelian.Ext ((presheafToSheaf _ _).obj
105	    ((yoneda ⋙ (Functor.whiskeringRight _ _ _).obj (ModuleCat.free k)).obj X)) F n
106	
107	/-- Phase A step 6 *Path 2* (iter-015): the `H⁰` algebraic bridge for `HModule'`,
108	mirroring iter-010's `HModule_zero_linearEquiv` for the iter-014 `HModule'`. The
109	$k$-linear identification of `HModule' k F 0 X` with the Hom group from the
110	sheafified representable `(presheafToSheaf _ _).obj ((yoneda ⋙ ModuleCat.free k).obj X)`.
111	Mathlib provides `CategoryTheory.Abelian.Ext.linearEquiv₀ : Ext X Y 0 ≃ₗ[R] (X ⟶ Y)`
112	in any `Linear R`-enriched abelian category; specialised to `R = k` and to the
113	`Linear k`-enriched abelian category `Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k)` (the `Linear k`
114	enrichment is auto-inferable from `HasSheafify J (ModuleCat.{u} k)` via Mathlib's
115	`Sheaf.linear`), this collapses `HModule' k F 0 X` to a `k`-linear Hom group. The
116	closure body is `Abelian.Ext.linearEquiv₀`; probe-confirmed one-liner (iter-015
117	plan-agent). Used downstream as the algebraic prerequisite for Stein-factorization-
118	derived `H⁰(C, O_C) ≃ k` on a connected proper `k`-curve (multi-iteration; queued
119	iter-017+ alongside the Mayer-Vietoris LES of iter-016+). -/
120	noncomputable def HModule'_zero_linearEquiv
121	    (k : Type u) [Field k]
122	    {C : Type v} [Category.{u, v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
123	    [HasWeakSheafify J (Type u)] [HasSheafify J (ModuleCat.{u} k)]
124	    [HasExt (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k))]
125	    (F : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k)) (X : C) :
126	    HModule' k F 0 X ≃ₗ[k]
127	      ((presheafToSheaf _ _).obj
128	        ((yoneda ⋙ (Functor.whiskeringRight _ _ _).obj (ModuleCat.free k)).obj X) ⟶ F) :=
129	  Abelian.Ext.linearEquiv₀
130	
131	/-- Iter-038 `Module.Finite` H⁰ transport companion for `HModule k F 0`. The iter-010
132	H⁰ bridge `HModule_zero_linearEquiv : HModule k F 0 ≃ₗ[k] ((constantSheaf J _).obj
133	(ModuleCat.of k k) ⟶ F)` identifies the degree-zero cohomology with a `k`-linear Hom
134	group; Mathlib's `Module.Finite.equiv` then transports `Module.Finite k`-ness across.
135	The `.symm` is required: iter-010's bridge has `HModule k F 0` on the LHS and the
136	Hom group on the RHS, but we want the Hom hypothesis on the LHS and the
137	`HModule` conclusion on the RHS, so we apply `.symm` first. Mirrors iter-037's
138	`module_finite_HModule_of_HModule'_X₄` pattern at degree $0$, with no Mayer-Vietoris
139	machinery required. Used downstream as a building block for `Module.Finite k
140	(HModule k (toModuleKSheaf C) 0)` once the Hom-from-constant-sheaf finiteness
141	input is supplied for proper geometrically integral $k$-curves. -/
142	theorem module_finite_HModule_zero
143	    (k : Type u) [Field k]
144	    {C : Type v} [Category.{u, v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
145	    [HasSheafify J (ModuleCat.{u} k)] [HasExt (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k))]
146	    (F : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k))
147	    [Module.Finite k ((constantSheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k)).obj (ModuleCat.of k k) ⟶ F)] :
148	    Module.Finite k (HModule k F 0) :=
149	  Module.Finite.equiv (HModule_zero_linearEquiv k F).symm
150	
151	/-- Iter-038 `Module.Finite` H⁰ transport companion for `HModule' k F 0 X`. Parallel
152	of `Scheme.module_finite_HModule_zero` for the iter-014 sheaf-parameterised carrier
153	`HModule'`. The iter-015 H⁰ bridge `HModule'_zero_linearEquiv : HModule' k F 0 X ≃ₗ[k]
154	((presheafToSheaf _ _).obj ((yoneda ⋙ ModuleCat.free k).obj X) ⟶ F)` identifies the
155	degree-zero open-evaluation cohomology with a `k`-linear Hom group from the sheafified
156	representable; Mathlib's `Module.Finite.equiv` then transports `Module.Finite k`-ness
157	across. The `.symm` is required for the same orientation reason as in
158	`Scheme.module_finite_HModule_zero`. -/
159	theorem module_finite_HModule'_zero
160	    (k : Type u) [Field k]
161	    {C : Type v} [Category.{u, v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
162	    [HasWeakSheafify J (Type u)] [HasSheafify J (ModuleCat.{u} k)]
163	    [HasExt (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k))]
164	    (F : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k)) (X : C)
165	    [Module.Finite k ((presheafToSheaf _ _).obj
166	        ((yoneda ⋙ (Functor.whiskeringRight _ _ _).obj (ModuleCat.free k)).obj X) ⟶ F)] :
167	    Module.Finite k (HModule' k F 0 X) :=
168	  Module.Finite.equiv (HModule'_zero_linearEquiv k F X).symm
169	
170	/-- Iter-039 curve specialisation of iter-038's `module_finite_HModule_zero` to
171	the structure sheaf `Scheme.toModuleKSheaf C` of a `Spec k`-scheme `C`. The
172	Grothendieck topology `Opens.grothendieckTopology C.left.toTopCat` is auto-inferred
173	via the iter-005 instances `instHasSheafify_Opens_ModuleCatK` and
174	`instHasExt_Sheaf_Opens_ModuleCatK`. The sheaf argument is inferred from the
175	result type. Mirrors iter-030 / iter-035 / iter-036 / iter-037's `_curve`
176	patterns. Used downstream as a building block for `Module.Finite k (HModule k
177	(toModuleKSheaf C) 0)` once the Hom-from-constant-sheaf finiteness input is
178	supplied for proper geometrically integral $k$-curves (typically the morally
179	trivial `H^0(C, O_C) ≃ k` from Stein factorization on a connected proper
180	curve). -/
181	theorem module_finite_HModule_zero_curve
182	    (k : Type u) [Field k]
183	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
184	    [Module.Finite k
185	      ((constantSheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology C.left.toTopCat) (ModuleCat.{u} k)).obj
186	        (ModuleCat.of k k) ⟶ Scheme.toModuleKSheaf C)] :
187	    Module.Finite k (Scheme.HModule k (Scheme.toModuleKSheaf C) 0) :=
188	  Scheme.module_finite_HModule_zero k _
189	
190	/-- Iter-039 curve specialisation of iter-038's `module_finite_HModule'_zero` to
191	the structure sheaf `Scheme.toModuleKSheaf C` of a `Spec k`-scheme `C`,
192	evaluated at an arbitrary open `U` of the underlying topological space. Parallel
193	of `module_finite_HModule_zero_curve` for the iter-014 sheaf-parameterised
194	carrier `HModule'`.  Same auto-inferred topology / instance setup. The open `U`
195	is an explicit parameter (unlike the implicit topology); the sheaf argument is
196	inferred. Used downstream in the cover-evaluation chain for proper geometrically
197	integral $k$-curves: for each affine corner $X_i$ of an `AffineCoverMVSquare`,
198	the iter-039 transport propagates `Module.Finite k`-ness from the Hom group
199	`((presheafToSheaf _ _).obj ((yoneda ⋙ free_k).obj X_i) ⟶ toModuleKSheaf C)` —
200	morally `Module.Finite k (Γ(X_i, O_C))` for affine $X_i$ — to the H⁰ cohomology
201	piece `HModule' k (toModuleKSheaf C) 0 X_i`. -/
202	theorem module_finite_HModule'_zero_curve
203	    (k : Type u) [Field k]
204	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
205	    (U : TopologicalSpace.Opens C.left.toTopCat)
206	    [Module.Finite k
207	      ((presheafToSheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology C.left.toTopCat) (ModuleCat.{u} k)).obj
208	        ((yoneda ⋙ (Functor.whiskeringRight _ _ _).obj (ModuleCat.free k)).obj U) ⟶
209	          Scheme.toModuleKSheaf C)] :
210	    Module.Finite k (Scheme.HModule' k (Scheme.toModuleKSheaf C) 0 U) :=
211	  Scheme.module_finite_HModule'_zero k _ U
212	
213	/-- Iter-040 affine cohomology vanishing carrier predicate. Packages the
214	geometric statement that for every affine open `U` of `C.left.toTopCat` and
215	every degree `i > 0`, the open-evaluation cohomology `Scheme.HModule' k F i U`
216	is the zero `k`-module (formulated as `Subsingleton`, since `HModule'` returns
217	a `Type u` rather than a `ModuleCat` object — see iter-014 abbrev). The class
218	is the affine-vanishing input the cover-evaluation chain consumes once the
219	producer instance is supplied (queued for iter-041+; multi-iteration
220	project-local construction expected since Mathlib does not yet provide
221	scheme-level Serre vanishing on affines for the `ModuleCat k`-flavour). -/
222	class IsAffineHModuleVanishing
223	    (k : Type u) [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
224	    (F : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology C.left.toTopCat) (ModuleCat.{u} k)) :
225	    Prop where
226	  subsingleton_HModule' : ∀ {U : TopologicalSpace.Opens C.left.toTopCat},
227	    AlgebraicGeometry.IsAffineOpen U → ∀ i, 0 < i →
228	      Subsingleton (Scheme.HModule' k F i U)
229	
230	/-- Iter-040 immediate consumer of `IsAffineHModuleVanishing`: given the
231	class hypothesis, the open-evaluation cohomology `HModule' k F i U` is
232	`Module.Finite k` for any affine open `U` and any `i > 0`. The proof unfolds
233	the class field to `Subsingleton (HModule' k F i U)` and then invokes
234	Mathlib's auto-derived `Subsingleton M → Module.Finite R M` instance (any
235	subsingleton module is finitely generated by the empty set, hence finite).
236	This consumer is the building block for the cover-evaluation chain: combined
237	with iter-039's `H^0` curve specialisations and iter-037's general-degree
238	corner-bridge transport, it closes the algebraic side of `Module.Finite k
239	(HModule k (toModuleKSheaf C) 1)` once the producer instance for
240	`IsAffineHModuleVanishing` is supplied. -/
241	theorem module_finite_HModule'_of_isAffineHModuleVanishing
242	    (k : Type u) [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
243	    (F : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology C.left.toTopCat) (ModuleCat.{u} k))
244	    [IsAffineHModuleVanishing k C F]
245	    {U : TopologicalSpace.Opens C.left.toTopCat}
246	    (hU : AlgebraicGeometry.IsAffineOpen U) (i : ℕ) (hi : 0 < i) :
247	    Module.Finite k (Scheme.HModule' k F i U) :=
248	  have : Subsingleton (Scheme.HModule' k F i U) :=
249	    IsAffineHModuleVanishing.subsingleton_HModule' (F := F) hU i hi
250	  inferInstance
251	
252	/-- Iter-043 wholespace H⁰ Hom-finiteness carrier predicate. Packages the
253	algebraic statement that the global Hom group
254	`((constantSheaf _).obj (ModuleCat.of k k) ⟶ F)` is finite over `k`. Morally
255	`Γ(C.left, F)` (the **global** sections of `F`) being finite over `k`. On a
256	proper geometrically integral $k$-curve $C$ with $F = O_C$, this is
257	$\Gamma(C, O_C) \simeq k$ (Stein factorization on a proper geometrically
258	connected curve), so this class admits a producer instance from the
259	geometric content of $C$ (supplied at iter-046).
260	
261	**Historical note on the abandoned per-affine-open variant.** An earlier
262	iter-041 attempt packaged Hom-finiteness of
263	`((presheafToSheaf _ _).obj ((yoneda ⋙ free k).obj U) ⟶ F)` **for every
264	affine open** `U`. By Yoneda + free-functor + sheafify adjunctions this
265	Hom group is `≃ₗ[k] Γ(U, F)`, and on a proper smooth $k$-curve $C$ with
266	$F = O_C$, $\Gamma(U, O_C)$ is **NOT finite over $k$** for $U$ a proper
267	affine open — e.g. for the standard cover of $\mathbb{P}^1_k$ by
268	$U_0 = U_1 = \mathbb{A}^1_k$, $\Gamma(U_i, O_{\mathbb{P}^1}) = k[t]$ is
269	infinite over $k$. That per-open class therefore admits no producer
270	instance on a non-trivial proper curve and has been deleted as dead
271	scaffolding.
272	
273	This wholespace version captures only the **global** Hom group, which on
274	a proper curve is finite via Stein. Iter-044+ LES finite-length transport
275	uses this wholespace class (in conjunction with iter-040's H>0 affine
276	vanishing). -/
277	class IsHModuleHomFinite
278	    (k : Type u) [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
279	    (F : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology C.left.toTopCat) (ModuleCat.{u} k)) : Prop where
280	  module_finite_hom : Module.Finite k
281	    ((constantSheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology C.left.toTopCat)
282	        (ModuleCat.{u} k)).obj (ModuleCat.of k k) ⟶ F)
283	
284	/-- Iter-043 immediate consumer: with the wholespace H⁰ Hom-finiteness class
285	hypothesis in scope, transport via iter-038's `module_finite_HModule_zero`
286	(which transports `Module.Finite k`-ness across iter-010's H⁰ algebraic bridge
287	`HModule_zero_linearEquiv : HModule k F 0 ≃ₗ[k] ((constantSheaf _).obj _ ⟶ F)`)
288	to obtain `Module.Finite k (HModule k F 0)`. Works at the global level
289	(one Hom-finiteness instance, not one per affine open). -/

309	/-- Iter-044 geometric Stein input for the iter-043 wholespace H⁰
310	Hom-finiteness carrier. For `C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))` an
311	integral $k$-scheme with proper structure morphism, the global sections
312	$\Gamma(C, O_C)$ form a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space.
313	
314	This is Stein's classical statement, packaged via Mathlib's
315	`AlgebraicGeometry.finite_appTop_of_universallyClosed`
316	(`Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Morphisms/Proper.lean`):
317	for $X$ integral and $f \colon X \to \Spec K$ universally closed and
318	locally of finite type, the structure-morphism ring map `f.appTop`
319	is module-finite. `IsProper f` packages both `UniversallyClosed f` and
320	`LocallyOfFiniteType f`.

323	`Module.Finite k (C.left.presheaf.obj (op ⊤))` (where the algebra
324	structure on `Γ(C, ⊤)` is iter-006's `kToSection`-derived) uses
325	`RingHom.finite_algebraMap` plus `Module.Finite.of_equiv_equiv` to
326	transport the base ring from intermediate `Γ(Spec k, ⊤)` to `k` along
327	the ring iso `Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of k)`. The compatibility
328	of algebra maps reduces to showing
329	`kToSection C (op ⊤).hom = (C.hom.appTop.hom).comp (Scheme.ΓSpecIso _).inv.hom`,
330	which collapses via `Subsingleton.elim` on the `⊤ ⟶ ⊤` hom-set +
331	`Functor.map_id`.

334	`IsHModuleHomFinite k C (toModuleKSheaf C)` via lifting Mathlib's
335	`constantSheafΓAdj.homEquiv` to a `LinearEquiv` + identification of
336	`Sheaf.Γ.obj (toModuleKSheaf C)` with the underlying global sections
337	+ transport via `Module.Finite.equiv`. -/
338	theorem module_finite_globalSections_of_isProper
339	    (k : Type u) [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
340	    [IsIntegral C.left] [IsProper C.hom] :
341	    Module.Finite k (C.left.presheaf.obj (Opposite.op ⊤)) := by
342	  have hf : (C.hom.appTop.hom).Finite :=
343	    AlgebraicGeometry.finite_appTop_of_universallyClosed k C.hom
344	  letI alg2 : Algebra ((Spec (CommRingCat.of k)).presheaf.obj (Opposite.op ⊤))
345	               (C.left.presheaf.obj (Opposite.op ⊤))
346	    := RingHom.toAlgebra C.hom.appTop.hom
347	  have hM_inter :
348	      Module.Finite ((Spec (CommRingCat.of k)).presheaf.obj (Opposite.op ⊤))
349	        (C.left.presheaf.obj (Opposite.op ⊤)) := by
350	    rw [← RingHom.finite_algebraMap]; exact hf
351	  refine Module.Finite.of_equiv_equiv
352	    (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of k)).commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv
353	    (RingEquiv.refl _) ?_
354	  ext x
355	  simp only [RingHom.coe_comp, RingEquiv.coe_toRingHom, RingEquiv.refl_apply,
356	    Function.comp_apply, RingHom.algebraMap_toAlgebra]
357	  have h_kts : (Scheme.toModuleKSheaf.kToSection C (Opposite.op ⊤)).hom =
358	                (C.hom.appTop.hom).comp ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of k)).inv.hom) := by
359	    ext y
360	    simp only [Scheme.toModuleKSheaf.kToSection, CommRingCat.hom_comp,
361	      RingHom.coe_comp, Function.comp_apply]
362	    exact congrFun (congrArg (·.hom) (C.left.presheaf.map_id (Opposite.op (⊤ :
363	                TopologicalSpace.Opens C.left.toTopCat)))) _
364	  calc (CommRingCat.Hom.hom (Scheme.toModuleKSheaf.kToSection C (Opposite.op ⊤)))
365	        ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of k)).commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv x)
366	       = (C.hom.appTop.hom).comp ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of k)).inv.hom)
367	          ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of k)).commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv x) :=
368	              congrFun (congrArg DFunLike.coe h_kts) _
369	    _  = C.hom.appTop.hom x := by
370	        simp only [RingHom.coe_comp, Function.comp_apply]
371	        congr 1
372	        change ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of k)).hom ≫
373	              (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of k)).inv).hom x = x
374	        rw [Iso.hom_inv_id]; rfl

8	/-!
9	# The 2-cover Čech cokernel `Ȟ¹(D)` for adelic Riemann–Roch (nodes N5–N7)
10	
11	This file is part of the **adelic Riemann–Roch lane** (see the lane design document).
12	It realises the degree-`1` cohomology of a curve as the concrete cokernel of a
13	two-chart cover — the algebraic incarnation of Weil's repartition quotient
14	`A_K / (A_K(D) + K)`.
15	
16	## The bridge from genus `H¹` to the Čech `H¹` (node N6)
17	
18	The project's genus carrier is `H¹(C, 𝒪_C) = HModule k (toModuleKSheaf C) 1`.
19	For a cover `𝒰` of `C` with `⨆ 𝒰 = ⊤` that is a **good** (Leray) cover — i.e. one
20	for which the Čech-to-derived comparison `HasCechToHModuleIso F 𝒰` holds — there is a
21	`k`-linear identification
22	```
23	HModule k F 1  ≃ₗ[k]  cechCohomology C F 𝒰 1,
24	```
25	obtained by chaining the comparison iso `cechToHModuleIso` (iter-050) with the
26	universe bridge `HModule'_eq_HModule_linearEquiv` (iter-034) at the terminal open
27	`⊤ = ⨆ 𝒰`.  This is `hModuleOne_linearEquiv_cechCohomology`.
28	
29	The hypothesis `HasCechToHModuleIso F 𝒰` is the existing project **gate** (a
30	single-field `Prop` class with no unconditional instance for a 2-affine cover of a
31	positive-genus curve): the equivalence is delivered *conditional* on that class,
32	exactly as the design intends.  Note that `IsCechAcyclicCover F 𝒰` for the whole
33	curve is **not** available (nor true) here: for a genus-`g` curve the degree-`1`
34	Čech cohomology of a 2-affine cover is `k^g ≠ 0`, so it is deliberately *not*
35	assumed — the comparison `HasCechToHModuleIso` (which does *not* force the
36	cohomology to vanish) is the correct and honest hypothesis.
37	
38	## The concrete section-level cokernel (node N5 target, definition)
39	
40	For a bundled 2-affine cover `S : X.AffineCoverMVSquare` and a sheaf `F` of
41	`k`-modules, the **difference-of-restrictions** map
42	```
43	δ : Γ(U₁, F) × Γ(U₂, F) →ₗ[k] Γ(U₁ ⊓ U₂, F),   (a, b) ↦ a|_{U₁∩U₂} − b|_{U₁∩U₂}
44	```
45	is `AffineCoverMVSquare.sectionDiff`.  Its cokernel `AffineCoverMVSquare.H1Cok`
46	is the concrete `Ȟ¹`, and its kernel `AffineCoverMVSquare.sectionGlue` is the
47	`H⁰ = L(D)` sheaf-gluing space (global sections `= { f : agree on the overlap }`).
48	
49	Because `F` is an arbitrary sheaf of `k`-modules, `H1Cok S F` is *already* the
50	divisor-twisted `Ȟ¹(D)`: specialising `F := 𝒪_C(D)` once N3's `sectionOfDivisor`
51	lands recovers the `H¹(D)` of the χ-ledger.
52	
53	## The concrete 2-cover family and the N6 bridge on it (this wave)
54	
55	`AffineCoverMVSquare.coverFamily : ULift (Fin 2) → Opens X` packages `U₁, U₂` as the
56	`Type u`-indexed family that `Scheme.cechCohomology` / the N6 bridge consume, with
57	`iSup_coverFamily : ⨆ i, S.coverFamily i = ⊤` the family-form of the cover totality.
58	`hModuleOne_linearEquiv_cechCohomology_coverFamily` then lands the N6 bridge on this
59	concrete family: `HModule k F n ≃ₗ[k] cechCohomology C F S.coverFamily n` (gated on
60	`HasCechToHModuleIso F S.coverFamily`).  Chaining node N5 (below) into this at `n = 1`
61	gives the lane's consumable corollary `HModule k F 1 ≃ₗ[k] H1Cok S F`.
62	
63	## The N5 identification `cechCohomology C F S.coverFamily 1 ≃ₗ[k] H1Cok S F` (PROVED)
64	
65	The in-tree `cechCohomology` is the homology of Mathlib's **unnormalized**
66	`cechComplexFunctor` (`FormalCoproduct.cochainComplexFunctor` of the Čech nerve): in
67	degree `n` the product runs over **all** `Fin (n+1) → ι` (not just increasing
68	multi-indices), and the differential `dⁿ = ∑_{i} (-1)^i δⁱ` is the alternating sum of
69	the cosimplicial cofaces `δⁱ = evalOp(P)(mapPower δ_i)` (a `Pi.lift` of projections to
70	`x ∘ δ_i` followed by the restriction `P(⨅ U∘(x∘δ_i)) → P(⨅ U∘x)`).  For the 2-element
71	cover (`ι = ULift (Fin 2)`) this is
72	```
73	  M⁰ = Γ(U₀) × Γ(U₁)                         (indices Fin 1 → ι)
74	  M¹ = Γ(U₀) × Γ(U₀₁) × Γ(U₀₁) × Γ(U₁)       (indices (0,0),(0,1),(1,0),(1,1))
75	  M² = ∏ over the 8 indices Fin 3 → ι         (incl. the degenerate diagonals)
76	```
77	where `Γ(U₀₁) = Γ(U₀ ⊓ U₁)`, and the two diagonal factors of `M¹` are the degenerate
78	cofaces `U_i ⊓ U_i = U_i`.  Writing a degree-1 cochain as `(p, q, r, s)`:
79	
80	* `d⁰(a, b) = (0, b|₀₁ − a|₀₁, a|₀₁ − b|₀₁, 0)`, so
81	  `im d⁰ = { (0, w, −w, 0) : w ∈ range (S.sectionDiff F) }` (note `w = b|₀₁ − a|₀₁` and
82	  `sectionDiff (a,b) = a|₀₁ − b|₀₁ = −w`, whence the images coincide as subgroups);
83	* `(d¹ n)_{(x₀,x₁,x₂)} = n_{(x₁,x₂)}| − n_{(x₀,x₂)}| + n_{(x₀,x₁)}|`.  The eight
84	  components force, after restriction (each triple intersection collapses to `U₀`, `U₁`
85	  or `U₀ ⊓ U₁`): the diagonals `p = s = 0` (from `x = (0,0,0)` and `(1,1,1)`) and
86	  `r = −q` (from `x = (0,1,0)` / `(1,0,1)`), the remaining four being automatic.  Hence
87	  `ker d¹ = { (0, q, −q, 0) : q ∈ Γ(U₀₁) } ≅ Γ(U₀₁)` via `q`.
88	
89	Therefore `H¹ = ker d¹ / im d⁰ ≅ Γ(U₀ ⊓ U₁) / range (S.sectionDiff F) = H1Cok S F`, the
90	iso being `[(0, q, −q, 0)] ↦ [q]`.  The identification is **unconditional** (no
91	acyclicity hypothesis — it is a pure homological-algebra fact about this specific
92	2-cover complex), and it is carried out in full in this file:
93	
94	* `sectionRestrict_trans`/`sectionRestrict_self`/`restrict_map_comp`/
95	  `restrict_map_self`/`isIso_restrict_map` — the poset restriction calculus every
96	  cancellation step reduces to;
97	* `cechD01`/`cechD12` with `cechD01_π`/`cechD12_π` — the low-degree differentials in
98	  product-typed, componentwise form;
99	* `overlapCocycle` with `overlapCocycle_comp_d` — the cocycle `q ↦ (0, q, −q, 0)`
100	  and the 8-index cancellation;
101	* `ker_cechD12_π_diag_zero₀`/`₁`, `ker_cechD12_π_off_diag`, `overlapKerEquiv` — the
102	  kernel description `ker d¹ = {(0, q, −q, 0)} ≃ₗ Γ(U₀ ⊓ U₁)`;
103	* `pairLift`/`pairProj`/`pairLift_comp_cechD01`/`map_range_pairDiff` — the image
104	  identification `im d⁰ = κ(im sectionDiff)`;
105	* `cechCohomologyOneEquivH1Cok` — node N5 proper, assembled through
106	  `isoSc' 0 1 2` and `ShortComplex.moduleCatHomologyIso`;
107	* `hModuleOneEquivH1Cok` — the N5+N6 consumable
108	  `HModule k F 1 ≃ₗ[k] H1Cok S F` under the `HasCechToHModuleIso` gate.
109	-/

119	/-! ## Node N6 — the `k`-linear bridge `HModule k F 1 ≃ₗ[k] cechCohomology C F 𝒰 1` -/
120	
121	/-- **Node N6 (bridge), abstract sheaf form.** For a sheaf `F` of `k`-modules on a
122	`Spec k`-scheme `C` and a cover `𝒰` with `⨆ 𝒰 = ⊤` satisfying the Čech-to-derived
123	comparison gate `HasCechToHModuleIso F 𝒰`, the genus-degree cohomology
124	`HModule k F n` is `k`-linearly identified with the Čech cohomology
125	`cechCohomology C F 𝒰 n` of the cover.
126	
127	The equivalence chains the iter-050 comparison
128	`cechToHModuleIso n : cechCohomology C F 𝒰 n ≃ₗ[k] HModule' k F n (⨆ 𝒰)` with the
129	iter-034 universe bridge `HModule'_eq_HModule_linearEquiv` at the terminal open
130	`⊤ = ⨆ 𝒰` (using `Preorder.isTerminalTop` transported along `h`, exactly the
131	iter-035 `HModule'_X₄_linearEquiv` pattern), then symmetrises.
132	
133	This is stated *conditional* on the `HasCechToHModuleIso` gate — no new `sorry` or
134	gate is introduced.  Downstream (`N5`, the finiteness keystone `N11`/`N12`) the
135	useful degree is `n = 1`: it reduces `H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` to the concrete Čech `H¹`. -/
136	noncomputable def hModuleOne_linearEquiv_cechCohomology
137	    {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))}
138	    (F : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology C.left.toTopCat) (ModuleCat.{u} k))
139	    {ι : Type u} (𝒰 : ι → TopologicalSpace.Opens C.left.toTopCat)
140	    [HasExt.{u} (Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology C.left.toTopCat) (ModuleCat.{u} k))]
141	    [HasExt.{u + 1} (Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology C.left.toTopCat) (ModuleCat.{u} k))]
142	    [HasCechToHModuleIso F 𝒰]
143	    (h : ⨆ i, 𝒰 i = ⊤) (n : ℕ) :
144	    HModule k F n ≃ₗ[k] cechCohomology C F 𝒰 n :=
145	  ((cechToHModuleIso n).trans
146	    (HModule'_eq_HModule_linearEquiv k F n
147	      (h.symm ▸ Preorder.isTerminalTop (TopologicalSpace.Opens C.left.toTopCat)))).symm
148	
149	/-- **Node N6 (bridge), curve specialisation.** Direct application of
150	`hModuleOne_linearEquiv_cechCohomology` to the structure sheaf
151	`F := Scheme.toModuleKSheaf C`.  Mirrors the iter-039/…/iter-050 `_curve` pattern
152	(dot-notation resolution against the structure sheaf), giving
153	`HModule k (toModuleKSheaf C) n ≃ₗ[k] cechCohomology C (toModuleKSheaf C) 𝒰 n`. -/
154	noncomputable def hModuleOne_linearEquiv_cechCohomology_curve
155	    {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
156	    {ι : Type u} (𝒰 : ι → TopologicalSpace.Opens C.left.toTopCat)
157	    [HasExt.{u} (Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology C.left.toTopCat) (ModuleCat.{u} k))]
158	    [HasExt.{u + 1} (Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology C.left.toTopCat) (ModuleCat.{u} k))]
159	    [HasCechToHModuleIso (Scheme.toModuleKSheaf C) 𝒰]
160	    (h : ⨆ i, 𝒰 i = ⊤) (n : ℕ) :
161	    HModule k (Scheme.toModuleKSheaf C) n
162	      ≃ₗ[k] cechCohomology C (Scheme.toModuleKSheaf C) 𝒰 n :=
163	  hModuleOne_linearEquiv_cechCohomology (Scheme.toModuleKSheaf C) 𝒰 h n

165	/-! ## Node N5 — the concrete 2-element cover family of an `AffineCoverMVSquare` -/

167	/-- **The 2-element open cover family `𝒰 : ULift (Fin 2) → Opens X` of an
168	`AffineCoverMVSquare`.** Indexed by `ULift.{u} (Fin 2)` (the `Type u` two-element
169	index that `Scheme.cechCohomology`/`hModuleOne_linearEquiv_cechCohomology` consume),
170	it sends the first index to `U₁` and the second to `U₂`.  This is the family whose
171	Čech cohomology `cechCohomology C F S.coverFamily 1` is identified with the concrete
172	cokernel `H1Cok S F` (node N5 proper) and fed into the N6 bridge. -/
173	noncomputable def AffineCoverMVSquare.coverFamily {X : Scheme.{u}} (S : X.AffineCoverMVSquare) :
174	    ULift.{u} (Fin 2) → TopologicalSpace.Opens X.toTopCat :=
175	  fun i => if i.down = 0 then S.U₁ else S.U₂
176	
177	@[simp] lemma AffineCoverMVSquare.coverFamily_zero {X : Scheme.{u}} (S : X.AffineCoverMVSquare) :
178	    S.coverFamily ⟨0⟩ = S.U₁ := rfl
179	
180	@[simp] lemma AffineCoverMVSquare.coverFamily_one {X : Scheme.{u}} (S : X.AffineCoverMVSquare) :
181	    S.coverFamily ⟨1⟩ = S.U₂ := rfl
182	
183	/-- **Cover totality of `coverFamily`.** The 2-element family covers `X`:
184	`⨆ i, S.coverFamily i = ⊤`.  This is the `ι → Opens`-family incarnation of the
185	`AffineCoverMVSquare.cover` field `U₁ ⊔ U₂ = ⊤`, and is the hypothesis
186	`hModuleOne_linearEquiv_cechCohomology` requires to land the N6 bridge on the whole
187	curve. -/
188	lemma AffineCoverMVSquare.iSup_coverFamily {X : Scheme.{u}} (S : X.AffineCoverMVSquare) :
189	    ⨆ i, S.coverFamily i = ⊤ := by
190	  refine le_antisymm le_top ?_
191	  have h : S.U₁ ⊔ S.U₂ ≤ ⨆ i, S.coverFamily i :=
192	    sup_le (le_iSup_of_le ⟨0⟩ (le_of_eq S.coverFamily_zero.symm))
193	      (le_iSup_of_le ⟨1⟩ (le_of_eq S.coverFamily_one.symm))
194	  exact S.cover ▸ h

197	`hModuleOne_linearEquiv_cechCohomology` to `S.coverFamily`, discharging the totality
198	hypothesis with `iSup_coverFamily`: for a sheaf `F` of `k`-modules on the curve `C`

203	`n = 1`) delivers the lane's consumable `HModule k F 1 ≃ₗ[k] H1Cok S F`. -/
204	noncomputable def AffineCoverMVSquare.hModuleOne_linearEquiv_cechCohomology_coverFamily
205	    {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))}
206	    (S : C.left.AffineCoverMVSquare)
207	    (F : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology C.left.toTopCat) (ModuleCat.{u} k))
208	    [HasExt.{u} (Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology C.left.toTopCat) (ModuleCat.{u} k))]
209	    [HasExt.{u + 1} (Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology C.left.toTopCat) (ModuleCat.{u} k))]
210	    [HasCechToHModuleIso F S.coverFamily]
211	    (n : ℕ) :
212	    HModule k F n ≃ₗ[k] cechCohomology C F S.coverFamily n :=
213	  hModuleOne_linearEquiv_cechCohomology F S.coverFamily S.iSup_coverFamily n

34	
35	Mathlib's `Abelian.Ext.chgUniv : Ext.{w} X Y n ≃ Ext.{w'} X Y n`

37	`Equiv` only. The iter-034 universe-bridge `HModule'_eq_HModule_linearEquiv`
38	(below in `section CoverTotality`) requires it as a `LinearEquiv` over the

41	transferred from the standard derived category through `homEquiv`, and
42	Mathlib's load-bearing intermediate lemma `Ext.homEquiv_chgUniv` (Basic.lean
43	L543–545) shows that `chgUniv` preserves the underlying derived-category
44	morphism. So `chgUniv` automatically commutes with `+` and `•`. Two short

53	/-- Iter-034 Mathlib gap-fill (a): `Abelian.Ext.chgUniv` is additive. The
54	underlying `homEquiv` (`Mathlib/Algebra/Homology/DerivedCategory/Ext/Basic.lean`
55	L162) is preserved by `chgUniv` (Mathlib lemma `Ext.homEquiv_chgUniv`,
56	L543–545), and the `AddCommGroup (Ext X Y n)` instance (L241–243) is defined by
57	transferring the `AddCommGroup` from the standard derived category through

60	private lemma Abelian.Ext.chgUniv_add
61	    {C : Type*} [Category C] [Abelian C]
62	    [HasExt.{w} C] [HasExt.{w'} C] {X Y : C} {n : ℕ} (a b : Abelian.Ext.{w} X Y n) :
63	    Abelian.Ext.chgUniv.{w'} (a + b) =
64	      Abelian.Ext.chgUniv.{w'} a + Abelian.Ext.chgUniv.{w'} b := by
65	  letI := HasDerivedCategory.standard C
66	  ext
67	  rw [Abelian.Ext.add_hom, ← Abelian.Ext.homAddEquiv_apply,
68	      ← Abelian.Ext.homAddEquiv_apply, ← Abelian.Ext.homAddEquiv_apply]
69	  change Abelian.Ext.homEquiv (Abelian.Ext.chgUniv.{w'} (a + b)) =
70	    Abelian.Ext.homEquiv (Abelian.Ext.chgUniv.{w'} a) +
71	      Abelian.Ext.homEquiv (Abelian.Ext.chgUniv.{w'} b)
72	  rw [Abelian.Ext.homEquiv_chgUniv, Abelian.Ext.homEquiv_chgUniv,
73	      Abelian.Ext.homEquiv_chgUniv, ← Abelian.Ext.add_hom]
74

76	is `Linear R`-enriched. Same proof shape as `chgUniv_add`, but using
77	`smul_hom` (`Mathlib/Algebra/Homology/DerivedCategory/Ext/Linear.lean` L52–55)
78	in place of `add_hom`. -/
79	private lemma Abelian.Ext.chgUniv_smul
80	    {R : Type*} [Ring R] {C : Type*} [Category C] [Abelian C] [Linear R C]
